chunks: 6 - He said: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Baseer al-Muqri informed me, saying: Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf narrated to me, from Abu Abdullah Zakariyya ibn Muhammad al-Mu'min, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, saying:

Indeed the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, was present at the deathbed of a young man. He said to him: "Say: There is no god but Allah." But his tongue was tied repeatedly. So he asked a woman near his head: "Does this one have a mother?" She said: "Yes, I am his mother." He said: "Are you displeased with him?" She said: "Yes, I have not spoken to him for six years." He said to her: "Be pleased with him." She said: "May Allah be pleased with him, O Messenger of Allah, with your pleasure."

Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said to him: "Say: There is no god but Allah." And he uttered it. Then the Prophet asked: "What do you see?" He said: "I see a man with a dark face, ugly appearance, dirty clothes, foul smell, who has drawn near me now and seized my throat."

So the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family, said to him: "Say: 'O He who accepts the little and forgives the much, accept from me the little and forgive me the much, for surely You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.'" The young man recited it. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, said: "Look, what do you see?" He said: "I see a man of bright complexion, handsome face, pleasant smell, fine clothes, who has drawn near me, and I see the dark one has turned away from me."
He said to him: "Repeat." So he repeated. Then he asked: "What do you see?" He said: "I no longer see the dark one, and I see the bright one has drawn near me." Then he passed away in that state.

key_terms.اعتقل لسانه: His tongue was tied - a sign of spiritual obstruction at death
key_terms.ساخطة: Displeased, angry - a mother's displeasure blocks spiritual ease
key_terms.طفي: He passed away, died - a classical Arabic expression for death
key_terms.كظم: Throat, windpipe - the dark figure strangling symbolizes spiritual torment

ai.seo_question: What happens when a mother is displeased with her child at the time of death in Islam?
ai.summary: This narrative from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) recounts how the Prophet (SAWW) attended a dying youth whose tongue was miraculously tied, preventing him from uttering the shahada. The Prophet discovered that the youth's mother had been displeased with him for six years. Once she forgave him at the Prophet's request, the youth could speak again. The Prophet then taught him a supplication, after which the youth's spiritual vision transformed from seeing a dark, terrifying figure to a bright, beautiful one. The hadith powerfully illustrates the devastating spiritual consequences of parental displeasure and the transformative power of divine supplication at the moment of death.
